To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lapatinib promotes atypical HER2:HER3 heterodimers that are distinct from the canonical HER2:HER2 active dimer, and that these dimers are able to cluster and respond cooperatively to neureglin, leading to a proliferative outcome.
lapatinib promotes atypical HER2–HER3 heterodimers, which are prone to neureglin responses.
HER3 is involved in the resistance to the HER2-targeted therapy, lapatinib, through an atypical HER2/HER3 heterodimers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of acquired resistance to HER2-targeted therapy and the development of new therapeutic strategies to overcome resistance.
the molecular mechanism of action of HER2 inhibitors, and in particular the role of the HER2-HER2 and HER2-HER1/HER3 heterodimers, in HER2-mediated breast cancer.
how the HER2 receptor is activated by the HER3 ligands and the implications of this for the development of resistance in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lapatinib-induced HER2 conformational change is responsible for the observed HER2-HER-3 heterodimerization.
HER2-HER2 and HER2-HER4 dimers are active and HER2-EGFR and HER2-VEGF dimers are not active.
the HER2-HER2 and HER2-HER1 dimer interfaces are distinct from the HER3-HER2 and the HER3-EGFR heterodimer interfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HER3 ligands and HER2 inhibitors cooperate to promote proliferation.
lapatinib can drive the formation of an atypical HER2/HER3 heterodimers that can promote cell proliferation in response to HER3 ligand stimulation.
lapatinib induces HER2-HER 3 dimerization and this promotes the proliferation through a novel heterodimer interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of kinase inhibitors in cancer therapy may have unanticipated effects on the conformational landscape of the target, which can lead to the emergence of resistance.
the HER2-HER2 and HER2-HER4 dimer interfaces are conserved in the HER2- HER3 dimer, which is not surprising since HER2-HER 4 is the closest related dimer to HER2-HER-3 in the HER family.
the use of kinase inhibitors to target the HER2 kinase domain can promote resistance to therapy by inducing a new dimer interface that is not targeted by inhibitors.
